prospects.thesis: Intel tops the composite screen with the strongest signal stack — bullish options flow, bullish institutional accumulation, and a +30% one-month move suggesting a genuine turnaround narrative is taking hold around its foundry business and government/CHIPS-related tailwinds. With yields rising and capital rotating toward tangible-asset semis with US manufacturing footprints, INTC is uniquely positioned versus fabless peers. Momentum plus smart money alignment justifies immediate exposure.

Lam is the cleanest way to play the semi-cap equipment cycle as HBM and advanced packaging capex accelerates into 2027, and its more modest +6.9% 1M move means we're not chasing an extended tape. Bullish options and institutional positioning confirm smart money is accumulating ahead of what should be a strong etch/deposition order cycle. Distinct sub-niche from INTC (equipment vs. IDM) supports diversification.

ARM's IP licensing model captures royalties across nearly every AI inference and mobile SoC being designed, and the +23.3% run reflects growing conviction in v9 royalty ramp and data center CPU wins. However, at 61.8x P/S the valuation demands patience — a pullback would offer far better risk/reward. Bullish options and institutional flow keep it on the radar.

SAIC provides much-needed defense-tech diversification at a compelling 0.7x P/S with bullish institutional positioning, offering a defensive counterweight to the momentum-heavy semi picks amid a rising VIX and climbing yields. As a prime IT services contractor to DoD and intelligence agencies, SAIC benefits from steady FY27 budget flow into digital modernization and AI-enabled mission systems. The flat 1M performance means we're entering before a re-rating rather than chasing.

GitLab offers pure-play exposure to AI-augmented software development via GitLab Duo, a distinct AI sub-niche from the hyperscaler/chip trades already saturating the watchlist. At 7.3x P/S with a -0.8% 1M print, it's the rare AI name not extended, and bullish options plus institutional accumulation suggest a setup ahead of enterprise seat expansion. Small $7.7B cap provides asymmetric upside if AI attach rates surprise.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: The most striking move is the stampede into Utilities — a put/call ratio of 0.05 with 3.4x normal volume means big money is essentially not buying any downside protection, they're just loading up on calls, which historically screams "AI power demand trade" as data center electricity buildouts get baked into rate cases and the administration keeps fast-tracking permitting reform and nuclear restarts. Pair that with heavy bullish flow in Financials (likely front-running continued deregulation, looser capital rules, and a friendlier M&A environment under the current SEC/FTC posture) and Technology (still riding the AI capex wave plus expectations that any tariff carve-outs will protect semiconductor supply chains), and you can see institutions positioning for a "easy money plus industrial policy" regime. On the flip side, Industrials and Healthcare are getting aggressively hedged — Industrials likely because tariff uncertainty and slowing global PMIs are starting to bite despite the reshoring narrative, and Healthcare because drug pricing executive orders, PBM scrutiny, and potential Medicaid cuts in the reconciliation bill are making managed care and pharma look politically radioactive. Historically this rotation pattern — defensives plus rate-sensitive plus tech leading, cyclicals lagging — is what you see in the 4-8 weeks before the market starts pricing in a growth slowdown and Fed cuts, so options desks are quietly telling you "soft landing narrative, but hedge the landing part." The contradiction worth noting: HYG's put/call is completely blown out and credit spreads are widening, which almost never coexists peacefully with bullish equity flow for long — somebody's wrong, and credit is usually the smarter room.
